jobs.title: Data Analyst - Active Secret Clearance Required
jobs.description:
MTSI is seeking a Data Analyst to support the USAF Test Pilot School at Edwards AFB, CA.

This position can be hybrid. It will require the ability and willingness to travel to Edwards AFB, CA up to 40%.

The Data Analyst provides mid-level data analysis and data-engineering support for Doolittle Labs’ flight-test campaigns and applied research. The Analyst executes day-to-day analysis under the technical direction of the Data Scientist and the Director of Data and Analytics, contributes to the lab’s data-driven test infrastructure buildout, and interfaces with OEM partners and external sponsors on post-event data.

Responsibilities and duties may include, but are not limited to:

Establish a “data-driven test” infrastructure and process for Doolittle Labs, aligned with the AFTC Multi-Domain Test Force (MDTF) and AFTC Data Working Group and VAULTIS-compliant for integration into the DAF Data Mesh Environment (DME).
Support all flight-test activities executed by Doolittle Labs, including modeling and simulation (M&S), test-data planning, and data acquisition requirements definition.
Support flight-test data analysis post-event, including data received from OEM partners (e.g., Lockheed Martin, RTX, Calspan, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, among others) and translation of OEM outputs into Doolittle Labs analysis products.
Apply data-analysis tools to quantify AI-agent performance early—in simulation, HITL/SITL, and pre-flight environments; before flight test on the X-62A VISTA.
Provide and disseminate flight-test results to Doolittle Labs leadership, sponsors, PAE/PM reach-back customers, and, where and when authorized and cleared, the broader T&E community.
Ensure that task related products are consistent in format and content with overall project deliverables - Routinely engage with Govt technical representative + tech leads for our teammates and subcontractors
Acts as a resource/mentor for colleagues with less experience
Works independently, with guidance in only the most complex situations

Required Skills

Working knowledge of applied statistical analysis, exploratory data analysis, and common machine-learning techniques as applied to engineering data.
Working knowledge of flight-test practices (test cards, telemetry, post-flight data reconstruction) is preferred, or a demonstrated ability to acquire that knowledge quickly.
Awareness of the DAF Data Strategy (VAULTIS, DME) and DCWF data-workforce framework; awareness of AFTC data-infrastructure activities led by the MDTF and AFTC Data Working Group.
Awareness of AI/autonomy T&E concepts sufficient to support Data Scientist and Director-level tasking, including basic V&V considerations for nondeterministic systems.
Proficiency with Python (e.g., pandas, NumPy, matplotlib) and SQL for data extraction, transformation, and analysis.
Working proficiency with a data-visualization platform (Tableau, Power BI, or plotly) sufficient to produce reviewable analysis products.
Working proficiency with MATLAB and/or Excel for engineering-data analysis; ability to work with structured telemetry files (CSV, HDF5, etc).
Experience with data cleaning, quality checks, ETL construction, and basic pipeline maintenance.
Skill in version control (e.g, Git) and reproducible-analysis practices (Jupyter, notebook standards

All MTSI employees are required to be skilled in the following core competencies:

Collaboration/Teamwork: Engages others across roles through communication and mutual respect, shares insights, enabling effective teamwork to ensure collective success. (teamwork)
Technical and Functional Skills: Leverages technical and functional expertise to deliver high performance, addresses challenges, and supports business needs while pursuing continuous skill development. (domain knowledge)
Entrepreneurialism: Fosters innovation, evaluates ideas, and advances initiatives with sound judgment and organizational awareness to drive growth and impact. (innovation)
Communication: Communicates clearly and effectively, fostering understanding, collaboration, and alignment through active listening and impactful messaging. (effective communication)
Customer Focus: Prioritizes customer needs, builds trust, and delivers exceptional service by using insights to drive improvements and strengthen relationships. (customer insight)

Required Experience

Minimum of 1-3 years of professional data-analysis, data-engineering experience, or comparable applied experience.

Desired Experience

Prior experience at AFTC, USAF Test Pilot School (TPS), TRMC, AFRL, DARPA, or an OEM flight-test organization.
Experience with X-62A VISTA, F-16 VENOM, Group 1-3 UAS, or similar AI-in-the-loop flight-test programs.
Familiarity with VAULTIS-compliant data products or DAF Data Mesh Environment integration.
Publication record in flight-test T&E, AI evaluation, or related peer-reviewed venues.
Familiarity with VAULTIS / DAF Data Mesh Environment data-product concepts.
Within driving distance of a SCIF preferred

Education Requirements

B.S. in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Aerospace or Systems Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related STEM discipline.

Travel

This position will require up to 40% travel to Edwards AFB, CA.

Clearance Requirements

Active Secret clearance is required
Ability to qualify for and maintain a TS/SCI clearance

U.S. Citizenship Is Required

The expected pay range for this position in California is $XXX,000/year to $XXX,000/year; however, base pay offered may vary depending on established government contract ranges, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, and other factors. MTSI also offers a full range of medical, financial, and other benefits, dependent on the position offered. Base pay information is based on market location. Applicants should apply via MTSI's internal or external careers site.

jobs.title: Pharmacy Program Coordinator - Specialty Pharmacy
jobs.description:
Job Description

Cedars-Sinai Medical Center is renowned for its excellence, tied #1 in California and appearing on the "Best Hospitals" Honor Roll for eleven years. The institution prides itself on its comprehensive healthcare services, with the Department of Pharmacy playing a vital role. Our pharmacy department has over 500 staff members who are dedicated on providing both inpatient and outpatient pharmacy services, ensuring that patients receive high-quality care tailored to their needs.

As a Specialty Pharmacist Program Coordinator at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, California, you will assist, under the direction of the Specialty Pharmacy Manager, and be accountable to the Specialty Pharmacy for all decisions affecting patients/ consumers. The pharmacist will assist in the development, and oversight of Specialty Pharmacy related programs, including operations and clinical-decision making aspects of the program, in the Specialty Pharmacy. The pharmacist is also responsible for ensuring required tasks are performed to maintain specialty pharmacy accreditation(s). The pharmacist is knowledgeable in the disease state management involving Specialty Pharmacy Medications.

Qualifications

Educational Requirements:

Pharm.D. or equivalent degree from an accredited school of pharmacy.
Completion of a PGY1 and/or PGY2 residency or equivalent practice experience.

License/Certification/Registration Requirements:

Current pharmacist licensure in the State of California.

What else are we looking for?

Completion of a PGY1 and/or PGY2 residency or equivalent practice experience.
Comprehensive knowledge of medical terminology as related to drug usage.
Comprehensive knowledge of common disease states and pathologies.
Ability to comprehend patient medical management plans.
Ability to assess and apply current pharmacological and biopharmaceutical principles for the selection and use of drug products in a clinical setting.
Ability to extract pertinent information from the patient or other sources and relate it to the patient care plan.
Possess the verbal and written communication skills required to fulfill the pharmacist’s responsibilities.
Ability to teach and serve as preceptor for training programs.
Ability to prepare drugs needed for immediate administration.
Ability to provide recommendations and monitor the use of drugs.
Knowledge of laws, regulations and standards relative to pharmacy practice.
Ability to adapt to change.
Ability to prioritize workflow.
Ability to evaluate medication regimens to meet the therapeutic needs of patients.
Ability to learn and adapt to the use of automated information systems in daily practice.
Demonstrated competency in techniques of pharmaceutical calculations, compounding and pharmacokinetics.
Possess patient-centered communication skills.
Possess computer skills necessary to perform job functions.
Exceptions to be approved by the Chief Pharmacy Officer or designee.

Physical Demands: (e.g., lifting, standing, walking)

Frequent standing, walking, bending, reaching, occasional sitting, pushing & pulling, lifting of materials up to 40 pounds for distances up to 10 feet

jobs.title: Voluntary Cleanup Program Site Manager (Hydrogeologist 3) Two Positions
jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring two Voluntary Cleanup Program Site Managers (Hydrogeologist 3)
within the Toxics Cleanup Program (TCP) .

Location:

Southwest Region Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day every other week is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by August 10, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Join a mission-driven team working to protect Washington’s communities by advancing cleanup of sites impacted by hazardous substances released to the environment. As a Site Manager in the Toxics Cleanup Program's southwest region, you will manage cleanup projects that enroll in the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP), ensuring cleanups meet the requirements of the Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA). You will evaluate complex geologic and environmental data, guide consultants and property owners toward technically sound cleanup actions, and help move contaminated sites to closure. If you are energized by applying geologic expertise to real-world cleanup projects, and want to make a direct and positive impact across the region, we would be thrilled to welcome your talent to our team.

What You Will Do

Review and evaluate technical reports, sampling data, work plans, scopes of work, and corrective-action proposals to identify regulatory compliance, data adequacy, and next steps for contaminated sites.
Conduct and document initial investigations and site hazard assessments, including data analysis, contamination evaluation, and preparation of clear written recommendations and assessment reports.
Provide technical oversight and geologic/hydrogeologic review of complex cleanup sites, including evaluating field activities, monitoring-well installation, and environmental sampling plans.
Prepare technical correspondence, opinion letters, regulatory determinations, and other cleanup documentation that clearly communicates requirements and supports cleanup progress.
Collaborate with property owners, consultants, community members, and local or state agencies to address technical issues, communicate expectations, and support productive, solution-focused interactions.
Offer technical assistance and mentorship to junior staff, contribute to peer reviews, and participate in program workgroups, planning efforts, and policy review as needed.
Maintain accurate site records and ensure timely data submittals and document uploads in agency databases to support tracking, reporting, and regulatory decision-making.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Possession
of a valid Washington State Geologist license and Hydrogeologist Specialty license AND

Seven years of experience
as a hydrogeologist, hydrologist, geologist or closely allied profession. Experience must include the following:

Regulatory and Cleanup Oversight: Experience reviewing environmental cleanup investigations and applying state cleanup regulations to support compliance and sound regulatory decisions.
Environmental Project Management: Skill in managing multiple contaminated-site projects, coordinating work plans and schedules, and ensuring steady progress toward cleanup completion.
Geologic and Environmental Data Interpretation: Ability to interpret geologic, hydrogeologic, and environmental data to evaluate site conditions and confirm that investigations are sufficient for decision-making.
Technical Communication and Documentation: Strong technical writing skills, including preparing clear, defensible reports, letters, and regulatory determinations.
Collaboration and Issue Resolution: Effective at working collaboratively with property owners, consultants, local governments, community members, and internal teams to resolve project issues.
Quality Assurance and Field Oversight: Experience evaluating field investigation activities, sampling plans, and data-quality practices, and maintaining accurate site records.
Technical Leadership and Mentorship: Ability to mentor junior staff and contribute to team consistency through peer review and knowledge-sharing.

Education:

major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

Examples of how to qualify -- a valid Washington State Geologist license and:

7 years of experience.
6 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
4 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
3 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
1 year of experience AND a Master’s degree.
A Ph.D.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Possession of a Washington State Geologist license.

NOTE:
Individuals who are interested in applying to this position, and believe they meet licensing requirements for the State of Washington based on reciprocity, are responsible for ensuring they meet licensing requirements for the State of Washington prior to submitting their application materials. These requirements can be found at the following website: WA State Licensing (DOL) Official Site: How to get your license: Geologists, engineering geologists, or hydrogeologists by reciprocity .

Desired Qualifications

Washington State Hydrogeologist Specialty License (or ability to obtain).
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training with current 8-hour refresher.
Advanced Environmental and Regulatory Interpretation: Demonstrated ability to analyze complex environmental, geologic, and regulatory information to develop clear, well-supported cleanup recommendations consistent with Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), Underground Storage Tank (UST) regulations, and related environmental laws.
Technical Communication and Engagement Skills: Strong ability to convey complex technical and regulatory concepts clearly in writing and verbally to support understanding, navigate challenging interactions, and guide cleanup progress.
Collaborative Problem Solving and Relationship Building: Experience working constructively with property owners, consultants, local governments, and agency staff to identify and resolve sensitive or complicated technical issues.
Senior-Level Technical Leadership: Experience providing technical guidance, peer review, or mentorship that strengthens team capability and supports consistent, science-based cleanup decisions.
Applied Cleanup Project and Technical Tools Experience: Proficiency managing contaminated site cleanup projects and using relevant software tools (e.g., Visio, Adobe applications, statistical tools, groundwater modeling platforms) to enhance the clarity, efficiency, and defensibility of technical evaluations.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. jobs.title: Streamflow Hydrologist (Hydrogeologist 2)
jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires field work. Mondays and Wednesdays are in office days, other days that do not involve field work can be teleworked.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by July 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education as described below:

Experience
: in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied profession

Experience must include
demonstrated competence in the following skill sets:

Teamwork & Collaboration – Ability to work respectfully and cooperatively with others to support shared goals and maintain productive working relationships.
Adaptability – Ability to adjust to changing field conditions, project demands, and new technologies to remain effective in varied situations.
Critical Thinking & Problem Solving – Ability to interpret information, troubleshoot issues, and make sound decisions to resolve problems and support program objectives.
Field Operations – Ability to plan, prepare for, and conduct fieldwork safely and effectively to collect accurate environmental data.
Hydrologic Measurement & Analysis - Ability to measure stream flow and channel characteristics to develop and update accurate stage-discharge rating curves.
Data Quality & Management – Ability to record, review, and maintain accurate data and notes to ensure data integrity and support scientific analyses. Ability to enter, validate, and analyze data using databases and standard office software to support accurate reporting.
Equipment & Vehicle Operation – Ability to safely operate field equipment, tools, vehicles, and/or boats to access sites and maintain monitoring stations.

Education:
involving a major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

Examples Of How To Qualify

6 years of experience.
5 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
4 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
3 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
2 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
a Master’s degree or higher.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license.

Desired Qualifications

Communication – Ability to clearly share information verbally and in writing to support accurate, effective, and professional interactions.
Workload & Time Management – Ability to plan, organize, and prioritize tasks to meet deadlines and maintain steady workflow.
Professional Conduct – Ability to maintain a calm, respectful, and professional demeanor to support a positive and inclusive work environment.
Project Coordination – Ability to organize field logistics, equipment, and schedules to support efficient and successful project execution.
Scientific Judgment – Ability to interpret environmental data and apply scientific principles to provide objective recommendations.
Hydrologic Monitoring– Ability to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot stream gages and related equipment to collect reliable hydrologic data.
Telemetry & Data Systems – Ability to install, operate, and maintain telemetry and data logger systems to support continuous data collection.
Environmental Sampling – Ability to use scientific instruments and sampling methods to collect water quality or biological data that support environmental assessments.

jobs.title: Global Industrial Automation Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
LotusWorks is an Engineering Services provider specializing in managing Commissioning, Construction Services, Calibration, Operations & Maintenance scopes of work within global manufacturing facilities. LotusWorks operates globally across EMEA and North America partnering with the world's leading manufacturers across the Semiconductor, Pharmaceutical & Biologics, Medical Device and Data Centre sectors. Our team of Engineering and Technical professionals is immersed in cutting-edge technologies and innovations. LotusWorks is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, integral to our people-first approach.

This role supports the global deployment of industrial automation initiatives by coordinating projects, standardizing execution, and collaborating with engineering, operations, and site stakeholders. The position combines program coordination with hands-on field support to ensure automation systems are successfully implemented and maintained across multiple facilities. The individual will work in both office and industrial environments while supporting the continuous improvement of automation programs worldwide.

Responsibilities

Manage project intake, prioritization, scheduling, and execution tracking for global industrial automation initiatives.
Coordinate project scope development, site assessments, proposals, and resource planning activities.
Develop and maintain project dashboards, forecasts, KPI reports, and performance metrics.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with stakeholders across multiple global sites.
Standardize automation deployment processes, templates, work packages, and project documentation.
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and program scalability.
Support installation, commissioning, and startup of industrial automation and monitoring systems.
Assist with low-voltage wiring, field device installation, control panel modifications, and sensor integration activities.
Perform field verification of instrumentation, sensors, transmitters, and automation equipment.
Support troubleshooting of PLC-based control systems, instrumentation circuits, and industrial communication networks.
Assist with vibration monitoring, predictive maintenance, and condition monitoring deployments.
Review control drawings, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, and instrumentation documentation to support project execution.
Conduct field walkdowns and equipment assessments to identify automation improvement opportunities.
Coordinate and support installation of sensors, transmitters, control devices, and communication infrastructure.
Support commissioning activities including loop checks, functional testing, system validation, and startup readiness.
Collaborate with engineering, maintenance, operations, and project teams to ensure successful project delivery.
Maintain project documentation, progress reports, commissioning records, and deployment status updates.
Support continuous improvement initiatives and standardization of global automation practices.
Ensure compliance with site safety requirements, company standards, and project specifications.
Any other duties or responsibilities that may be assigned to you in your role.

Skills Required

Experience in project coordination, project management, commissioning, operations, maintenance, industrial automation, electrical, or instrumentation environments.
Strong organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
Basic understanding of industrial control systems and instrumentation.
Experience with PLCs, SCADA, DCS, or industrial control systems.
Familiarity with instrumentation, sensors, transmitters, vibration monitoring, and predictive maintenance technologies.
Knowledge of low-voltage wiring, control panels, field devices, and commissioning activities.
Working knowledge of industrial networking protocols and Industrial IoT technologies.
Experience using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, Smartsheet, or similar reporting platforms.
Ability to review P&IDs, wiring diagrams, control drawings, and instrumentation documentation.
Willingness to work in both office and industrial field environments.
Semiconductor, facilities, commissioning, manufacturing, or industrial automation experience.
Strong problem-solving skills with a continuous improvement mindset.

Education / Licenses / Certifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Instrumentation Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field preferred.
Project Management certification preferred.
OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification preferred.
PLC, SCADA, or industrial automation certifications preferred.
Proof of education, licenses, and certifications will be required where applicable.

Benefits

Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
Life, Short-Term, Long-Term Disability Insurance
Training and Education Assistance
401k Retirement Plan
Extra Annual Leave with Years of Service
Maternity/Paternity Leave
Recognition Rewards

LotusWorks is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where all employees feel valued, respected, and empowered.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst - Active Secret Clearance Required
new_jobs.description:
MTSI is seeking a Data Analyst to support the USAF Test Pilot School at Edwards AFB, CA.

This position can be hybrid. It will require the ability and willingness to travel to Edwards AFB, CA up to 40%.

The Data Analyst provides mid-level data analysis and data-engineering support for Doolittle Labs’ flight-test campaigns and applied research. The Analyst executes day-to-day analysis under the technical direction of the Data Scientist and the Director of Data and Analytics, contributes to the lab’s data-driven test infrastructure buildout, and interfaces with OEM partners and external sponsors on post-event data.

Responsibilities and duties may include, but are not limited to:

Establish a “data-driven test” infrastructure and process for Doolittle Labs, aligned with the AFTC Multi-Domain Test Force (MDTF) and AFTC Data Working Group and VAULTIS-compliant for integration into the DAF Data Mesh Environment (DME).
Support all flight-test activities executed by Doolittle Labs, including modeling and simulation (M&S), test-data planning, and data acquisition requirements definition.
Support flight-test data analysis post-event, including data received from OEM partners (e.g., Lockheed Martin, RTX, Calspan, Boeing, Northrop Grumman, among others) and translation of OEM outputs into Doolittle Labs analysis products.
Apply data-analysis tools to quantify AI-agent performance early—in simulation, HITL/SITL, and pre-flight environments; before flight test on the X-62A VISTA.
Provide and disseminate flight-test results to Doolittle Labs leadership, sponsors, PAE/PM reach-back customers, and, where and when authorized and cleared, the broader T&E community.
Ensure that task related products are consistent in format and content with overall project deliverables - Routinely engage with Govt technical representative + tech leads for our teammates and subcontractors
Acts as a resource/mentor for colleagues with less experience
Works independently, with guidance in only the most complex situations

Required Skills

Working knowledge of applied statistical analysis, exploratory data analysis, and common machine-learning techniques as applied to engineering data.
Working knowledge of flight-test practices (test cards, telemetry, post-flight data reconstruction) is preferred, or a demonstrated ability to acquire that knowledge quickly.
Awareness of the DAF Data Strategy (VAULTIS, DME) and DCWF data-workforce framework; awareness of AFTC data-infrastructure activities led by the MDTF and AFTC Data Working Group.
Awareness of AI/autonomy T&E concepts sufficient to support Data Scientist and Director-level tasking, including basic V&V considerations for nondeterministic systems.
Proficiency with Python (e.g., pandas, NumPy, matplotlib) and SQL for data extraction, transformation, and analysis.
Working proficiency with a data-visualization platform (Tableau, Power BI, or plotly) sufficient to produce reviewable analysis products.
Working proficiency with MATLAB and/or Excel for engineering-data analysis; ability to work with structured telemetry files (CSV, HDF5, etc).
Experience with data cleaning, quality checks, ETL construction, and basic pipeline maintenance.
Skill in version control (e.g, Git) and reproducible-analysis practices (Jupyter, notebook standards

All MTSI employees are required to be skilled in the following core competencies:

Collaboration/Teamwork: Engages others across roles through communication and mutual respect, shares insights, enabling effective teamwork to ensure collective success. (teamwork)
Technical and Functional Skills: Leverages technical and functional expertise to deliver high performance, addresses challenges, and supports business needs while pursuing continuous skill development. (domain knowledge)
Entrepreneurialism: Fosters innovation, evaluates ideas, and advances initiatives with sound judgment and organizational awareness to drive growth and impact. (innovation)
Communication: Communicates clearly and effectively, fostering understanding, collaboration, and alignment through active listening and impactful messaging. (effective communication)
Customer Focus: Prioritizes customer needs, builds trust, and delivers exceptional service by using insights to drive improvements and strengthen relationships. (customer insight)

Required Experience

Minimum of 1-3 years of professional data-analysis, data-engineering experience, or comparable applied experience.

Desired Experience

Prior experience at AFTC, USAF Test Pilot School (TPS), TRMC, AFRL, DARPA, or an OEM flight-test organization.
Experience with X-62A VISTA, F-16 VENOM, Group 1-3 UAS, or similar AI-in-the-loop flight-test programs.
Familiarity with VAULTIS-compliant data products or DAF Data Mesh Environment integration.
Publication record in flight-test T&E, AI evaluation, or related peer-reviewed venues.
Familiarity with VAULTIS / DAF Data Mesh Environment data-product concepts.
Within driving distance of a SCIF preferred

Education Requirements

B.S. in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Aerospace or Systems Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related STEM discipline.

Travel

This position will require up to 40% travel to Edwards AFB, CA.

Active Secret clearance is required
Ability to qualify for and maintain a TS/SCI clearance

U.S. Citizenship Is Required

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring two Voluntary Cleanup Program Site Managers (Hydrogeologist 3)
within the Toxics Cleanup Program (TCP) .

Location:

Southwest Region Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Application Timeline

Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Join a mission-driven team working to protect Washington’s communities by advancing cleanup of sites impacted by hazardous substances released to the environment. As a Site Manager in the Toxics Cleanup Program's southwest region, you will manage cleanup projects that enroll in the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP), ensuring cleanups meet the requirements of the Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA). You will evaluate complex geologic and environmental data, guide consultants and property owners toward technically sound cleanup actions, and help move contaminated sites to closure. If you are energized by applying geologic expertise to real-world cleanup projects, and want to make a direct and positive impact across the region, we would be thrilled to welcome your talent to our team.

What You Will Do

Review and evaluate technical reports, sampling data, work plans, scopes of work, and corrective-action proposals to identify regulatory compliance, data adequacy, and next steps for contaminated sites.
Conduct and document initial investigations and site hazard assessments, including data analysis, contamination evaluation, and preparation of clear written recommendations and assessment reports.
Provide technical oversight and geologic/hydrogeologic review of complex cleanup sites, including evaluating field activities, monitoring-well installation, and environmental sampling plans.
Prepare technical correspondence, opinion letters, regulatory determinations, and other cleanup documentation that clearly communicates requirements and supports cleanup progress.
Collaborate with property owners, consultants, community members, and local or state agencies to address technical issues, communicate expectations, and support productive, solution-focused interactions.
Offer technical assistance and mentorship to junior staff, contribute to peer reviews, and participate in program workgroups, planning efforts, and policy review as needed.
Maintain accurate site records and ensure timely data submittals and document uploads in agency databases to support tracking, reporting, and regulatory decision-making.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Possession
of a valid Washington State Geologist license and Hydrogeologist Specialty license AND

Seven years of experience
as a hydrogeologist, hydrologist, geologist or closely allied profession. Experience must include the following:

Regulatory and Cleanup Oversight: Experience reviewing environmental cleanup investigations and applying state cleanup regulations to support compliance and sound regulatory decisions.
Environmental Project Management: Skill in managing multiple contaminated-site projects, coordinating work plans and schedules, and ensuring steady progress toward cleanup completion.
Geologic and Environmental Data Interpretation: Ability to interpret geologic, hydrogeologic, and environmental data to evaluate site conditions and confirm that investigations are sufficient for decision-making.
Technical Communication and Documentation: Strong technical writing skills, including preparing clear, defensible reports, letters, and regulatory determinations.
Collaboration and Issue Resolution: Effective at working collaboratively with property owners, consultants, local governments, community members, and internal teams to resolve project issues.
Quality Assurance and Field Oversight: Experience evaluating field investigation activities, sampling plans, and data-quality practices, and maintaining accurate site records.
Technical Leadership and Mentorship: Ability to mentor junior staff and contribute to team consistency through peer review and knowledge-sharing.

Education:

major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

Examples of how to qualify -- a valid Washington State Geologist license and:

7 years of experience.
6 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
4 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
3 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
1 year of experience AND a Master’s degree.
A Ph.D.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Possession of a Washington State Geologist license.

NOTE:
Individuals who are interested in applying to this position, and believe they meet licensing requirements for the State of Washington based on reciprocity, are responsible for ensuring they meet licensing requirements for the State of Washington prior to submitting their application materials. These requirements can be found at the following website: WA State Licensing (DOL) Official Site: How to get your license: Geologists, engineering geologists, or hydrogeologists by reciprocity .

Desired Qualifications

Washington State Hydrogeologist Specialty License (or ability to obtain).
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training with current 8-hour refresher.
Advanced Environmental and Regulatory Interpretation: Demonstrated ability to analyze complex environmental, geologic, and regulatory information to develop clear, well-supported cleanup recommendations consistent with Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), Underground Storage Tank (UST) regulations, and related environmental laws.
Technical Communication and Engagement Skills: Strong ability to convey complex technical and regulatory concepts clearly in writing and verbally to support understanding, navigate challenging interactions, and guide cleanup progress.
Collaborative Problem Solving and Relationship Building: Experience working constructively with property owners, consultants, local governments, and agency staff to identify and resolve sensitive or complicated technical issues.
Senior-Level Technical Leadership: Experience providing technical guidance, peer review, or mentorship that strengthens team capability and supports consistent, science-based cleanup decisions.
Applied Cleanup Project and Technical Tools Experience: Proficiency managing contaminated site cleanup projects and using relevant software tools (e.g., Visio, Adobe applications, statistical tools, groundwater modeling platforms) to enhance the clarity, efficiency, and defensibility of technical evaluations.

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires field work. Mondays and Wednesdays are in office days, other days that do not involve field work can be teleworked.

Application Timeline

Apply by July 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

Manage project intake, prioritization, scheduling, and execution tracking for global industrial automation initiatives.

Collaborate with engineering, maintenance, operations, and project teams to ensure successful project delivery.
Maintain project documentation, progress reports, commissioning records, and deployment status updates.
Support continuous improvement initiatives and standardization of global automation practices.
Ensure compliance with site safety requirements, company standards, and project specifications.

Experience in project coordination, project management, commissioning, operations, maintenance, industrial automation, electrical, or instrumentation environments.
Strong organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
Basic understanding of industrial control systems and instrumentation.
